You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data points to late 2013. Unemployment is 7.3%, which matches September or October 2013. The 10-year yield is 2.74% and US equities are up 30.1% over 12 months, which fits the end of 2013. Gold is down 27.8% over 12 months, also consistent with 2013.

To pin the month, headline CPI at 0.94% YoY is consistent with October 2013, which was 1.0%. Unemployment was 7.3% in October 2013 (and 7.2% in September), then 7.0% in November. The 3-month average payroll change of about 202k fits October (the October figure was 204k, with a revised average around 200k). Gold fell 6.9% in one month, which fits November 2013 (gold dropped from about 1325 to 1250). But the 10-year yield rose from 2.64% in October to 2.74% in November, which fits November's 2.74%. The 10-year yield at the end of October was 2.55%, so November fits better.

The unemployment rate would not be 7.3% for November, which was published as 7.0% in December. However, with the government shutdown, the October data came out in November and the November data in early December. The snapshot's "latest published" value at the end of November would still be the 7.3% October figure, so that is consistent with November.

US large-cap equity rose 2.7% in the month, which fits November 2013 (S&P up about 2.8%). The 3-month gain of 11.1% also fits.

I estimate November 2013.
